name: Cosmo First Ltd
title: Cosmo First Ltd - 508814 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Cosmo First Q1 FY27 consolidated sales rose 46% to Rs 1,166 crore and EBITDA 26% to Rs 147 crore, though margin fell to 12.6%.
summary.overview: Revenue growth was driven mainly by raw material pass-through after the West Asia conflict, with volume up only 9%. EBITDA rose 26% to Rs 147 crore, helped by better per-kg contribution across base, semi-specialty and specialty films, and management says all B2B businesses are now profitable. Export volumes fell 13% due to port congestion and a line maintenance outage, and BOPET margins compressed sharply sequentially. Net debt was flat at Rs 1,166 crore (2.3x EBITDA), and management targets below 2x within 12 months.

segments.name: BOPP films (base, semi-specialty, specialty)
segments.commentary: Specialty sales volume up 12% YoY; specialty mix at 61%, highest in five quarters, with target of 70%. Gross margin Rs 30/kg including non-repeating stock gain; management said base BOPP margin ex-stock gain was broadly flat.

segments.name: BOPET films
segments.commentary: Gross margin fell to Rs 9/kg from Rs 18/kg in Q4 FY26. Capacity is 30,000 tonnes against 277,000 tonnes of BOPP. Management expects margins to recover after recently levied anti-dumping duty.

segments.name: US film business
segments.commentary: Export volumes down 13% due to port congestion and in-transit shipments. US subsidiary received about USD 7 million duty refund in July 2026, not yet appropriated. Management expects US revenue to grow 25-30% in FY27.

segments.name: Specialty chemicals
segments.commentary: Revenue up 34% YoY with 25% EBITDA margin, improved 2 percentage points QoQ. About 80% of business is backward integration into group films. FY27 growth guided at about 50%; Rs 400-500 crore FY30 target may be reached by FY29.

segments.name: Cosmo Plastech (rigid packaging)
segments.commentary: Revenue up over 58% YoY and turned EBITDA positive. FY26 revenue about Rs 100 crore; FY27 guided Rs 150-160 crore and Rs 200+ crore next year, with capacity up 50% at minimal capex over next two quarters.

segments.name: Zigly (petcare)
segments.commentary: Monthly GMV run rate about Rs 100 crore (annualised Rs 100 crore, per the call). Gross margin 47%, services 64% of sales mix, private label revenue up 105% YoY, 47 centres, 29,000 customers in the quarter. Management estimates breakeven at about Rs 250 crore revenue, a couple of years away.

segments.name: Cosmo Consumer (window films, PPF, ceramic coatings)
segments.commentary: Near EBITDA breakeven in Q1. Revenue grew 4.5x last year and management expects more than 3x this year. Margin about 25% (EBIT per management, up from 15-17% at launch); gross margin target 35-40%. TV advertising began July 2026; 150 dealers in 100+ cities.

guidance_outlook: Consolidated topline to grow about 20% in FY27, with commensurate bottom-line growth.
New businesses to grow about 60% in FY27; specialty chemicals about 50%.
ROCE targeted at 15-20% within 12-24 months, from about 11% in the last financial year.
Net debt/EBITDA to fall below 2x within 12 months; Rs 400-500 crore debt reduction over two years with minimal capex.
Specialty mix target of 67-68% next year if 10% volume growth is achieved; management also cited 70% as an objective.
Renewable power savings of about Rs 25 crore per year not yet in Q1; one PPA from Q3 FY27, another from Q1 FY28.
capex_capacity: Film capacity utilisation at 85% in Q1 FY27; about 15% spare capacity expected to be filled over the next two quarters.
Plastech capacity to rise 50% over the next two quarters at minimal capex; revenue capacity of Rs 250+ crore.
Management says capex cycle is largely complete; Rs 1,200 crore strategic capex over the last three years. Future incremental capex directed to specialty assets.
BOPP capacity 277,000 tonnes; BOPET 30,000 tonnes. A line under maintenance in Q4 FY26 lost a couple of thousand tonnes of volume.
demand_pricing: Raw material prices rose sharply after the West Asia conflict; pass-through inflated revenue and working capital (Rs 85 crore).
Management said the spread on BOPP fluctuates daily; July spreads were broadly in line with Q1. Demand described as quite strong.
India is slightly over capacity in BOPET, which management expects to correct; anti-dumping duty recently levied.
Specialty film margins above Rs 60/kg for five consecutive quarters; semi-specialty about Rs 15-20/kg above base film margins.
PPF penetration in India about 2%, growing 30%; pet care market growing 22% a year.

qa_highlights.question: How will ROCE move over the next two years given new verticals are EBITDA positive, and what are the growth levers by business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ROCE was about 11% last year and is targeted at 15-20% within 12-24 months. Levers are volume growth (about 15% film capacity still to be sold), Plastech capacity +50% at minimal capex, consumer growth, and US revenue growth of 25-30% in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What new BOPP specialty grades were developed, and what per-kg margin uplift do they bring?
qa_highlights.answer: Specialty sales grew 12% in the quarter; launches included synthetic paper film, PVC-free green graphic films and anti-fog BOPET lidding films. Six patents are granted and 11 are pending. Semi-specialty runs Rs 15-20/kg above base, and specialty has been above Rs 60/kg for five quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margins lag revenue growth, and was the high crude-linked raw material cost passed through?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue rose 46% against 9% volume growth, with the gap attributed to raw material pass-through after the West Asia conflict. EBITDA per kg rose about 15%. Management said the BOPP base-margin stock gain is one-time, while BOPET margins should recover with anti-dumping duty.

qa_highlights.question: What is the utilisation of films, specialty chemicals and Plastech?
qa_highlights.answer: Film utilisation was 85% in Q1, with about 15% spare capacity expected to fill over two quarters. Specialty chemicals has 15-20% spare capacity. Plastech is adding 50% capacity, with revenue capacity of Rs 250+ crore, and management said specialty films can reach close to 90% without major capex.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Zigly path to breakeven and unit economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Zigly's loss widened to Rs 15 crore from Rs 10 crore as it invested ahead of revenue (four new centres, two hospital acquisitions, 20+ private labels). Loss as a share of revenue fell from 82% to 69%, gross margin is 47%, and services are 64% of mix. Breakeven is estimated at about Rs 250 crore revenue, a couple of years away.

qa_highlights.question: Why did US volumes fall 13%, and what was the capacity of the line under maintenance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited in-transit export volumes stuck at Indian ports (not booked until bill of lading), a maintenance outage on one line in the prior quarter, and a new line that started mid-Q1 last year. The line under maintenance was about a couple of thousand tonnes, and some volume is expected to recover in Q2.

risks_watch: Port congestion and in-transit export volumes: about USD 7m US duty refund not yet appropriated, and US volume recovery in Q2 is uncertain.
BOPET margin compression (Rs 9/kg from Rs 18/kg QoQ) and India being slightly over capacity in BOPET; anti-dumping duty effect needs to show up.
Net debt of Rs 1,166 crore (2.3x EBITDA) and working capital pressure from raw material pass-through (Rs 85 crore); target below 2x within 12 months.
Zigly loss widened to Rs 15 crore; breakeven at about Rs 250 crore revenue is a couple of years away.
Specialty mix target of 70% and 67-68% next year depends on 10% volume growth and spare capacity of about 15%.
Raw material availability and crude-linked price volatility; BOPP spreads fluctuate daily, July spreads broadly in line with Q1.
Renewable power savings of about Rs 25 crore per year not yet in Q1 numbers; first PPA from Q3 FY27, second from Q1 FY28.
key_quotes: June 2026Q reflects a quarter of continued momentum in our core flexible packaging business alongside newer businesses gaining scale and operational efficiencies resulting all our B2B businesses are now profitable.
The right margin is contribution per kilogram and that improved across every category.
Zigly breakeven should happen around Rs. 250 crores of revenue.
There is a good likelihood that by FY '29 itself, we will surpass this target.
Renewable power projected savings are yet to kick in.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the strategic story (specialty mix, new B2B businesses turning profitable, capex cycle complete) but cautious and sometimes evasive on specifics: it declined to give long-term consumer revenue or margin targets, said next-year growth is still being evaluated, and called BOPP spreads a daily fluctuation without numbers.

adds.what: Cosmo Plastech rigid packaging capacity up 50% at minimal capex (revenue capacity Rs 250+ crore)

growth.why: Management guides FY27 topline growth of about 20% (new businesses ~60%, specialty chemicals ~50%, Plastech Rs 150-160 crore), backed partly by ~15% film spare capacity to fill over two quarters and a 50% Plastech capacity increase, but Q1 growth was mostly raw-material pass-through with volume up only 9%, and no full order book was disclosed.
